question: Who among the following Mughal emperors was taken as the leader by the sepoys and led the revolt of 1857?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Bahadur Shah Zafar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Bahadur Shah Zafar:

 
 
• He was also known as Bahadur Shah-II.
 
• He was the last Mughal emperor of India who reigned from 1837-58.
 
• For most of his reign, he was a client of the British and was without real authority.
 
• He was chosen as a nominal leader of the revolt of 1857.
 
• After the rebellion, he was put down by the British, and was exiled to Rangoon__ in Burma(Myanmar) and later he died there. ​
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Muhammad Shah**

 
 
• Born on August 7, 1702, and died on April 26, 1748; Mirza Nasir-ud-Din Muḥammad Shah, also known as Muhammad Shah, was the 13th Emperor of the Mughal Empire in India.
 
• He ruled from 1719 to 1748 for a total of 29 years.
 
• He was known as Rangeela because of his luxurious life-style.
 
• Early in his reign, he was controlled by the Sayyid Brothers but eventually killed them with help from his advisor, Nizam-ul-Mulk.
 
• in 1724, Nijam-ul-Mulk became the Wazir and founded the independent Hyderabad state.
 
• Baji Rao 1 Maratha Peshwa invaded Delhi in 1737.
 
• His time as emperor saw the Mughal Empire weaken, facing both internal problems and attacks from outsiders like the Persian ruler Nader Shah in 1739.
 
• Nader Shah defeated the Mughals in the Battle of Karnal in 1739 and took away the Peacock Throne.
 
 
 
• Shah Jahan II
 
 
• Sayyid Brothers gave the title Shah Jahan II to Rafi-ud-Daula.
 
• He was an opium addict.
 
• He was the second son of Rafi-ush-Shan and a grandson of Bahadur Shah I.
 
• Shah Jahan II suffered from tuberculosis just like his younger brother.
 
• He was physically and mentally unfit to perform the duties of a ruler.
 
• He died on 17 September 1719 at Bidyapur. He was buried beside Rafi ud-Darajat at the dargah of Qutbuddin Bakhtiar Kaki at Mehrauli in Delhi.
 
 

 
• **Aurangzeb**
 
• The Mughal emperor Aurangzeb was known as Abul Muzaffar Muhi-ud-Din Muhammad Aurangzeb, commonly known as Aurangzeb or by his regional title Alamgir__.
 
 
• Mohi-ud-din Mohammed Aurangzeb was born on Oct. 24, 1618, at Dohad and was the third son of Emperor Shah Jahan.
 
• Aurangzeb (1618-1707) was the sixth Mogul emperor of India and the last of the "Great Moguls."
 
• He extended the Mogul Empire to its farthest boundaries, but his reign was harsh and marked by revolts.
 
• He ruled over most of the Indian subcontinent during some parts of his reign, which lasted for 49 years from 1658 until he died in 1707.
 
• Mughal emperor Aurangzeb died in 1707 after a 49-year reign without officially declaring a crown prince.
 
 

82
